about: PokeSquad Battler's Trainer teams: roles, archetypes, rules and tiers for every Stadium mode (Ranked, Link, Friendly and any added later). Edit it with 'PokeSquad Battler Team Config.html'; the game reads it when it's built (sh src/build.sh).

snow_veil_aurora_veil_offense.name: Snow · Aurora Veil setter (Aurora Veil offense)

ho_sweeper_dual_screens.name: Hyper Offense · sweeper (Dual Screens, Priority rush)

bo_intimidate_pivot_core.name: Bulky Offense · Intimidate user (Pivot core, Pledge core)

bo_pivot_intimidate_core.name: Bulky Offense · pivot (Intimidate core, Pledge core)

goodstuffs_fakeout.name: Fake Out + Intimidate · Fake Out user

archetypes.name: Rain
archetypes.plan: Rain Dance starts rain for 5 rounds (8 with a Damp Rock): Water moves hit ×1.5 and Fire moves ×0.5, Swift Swim doubles Speed, and Thunder and Hurricane never miss

subs.name: Swift Swim offense
subs.plan: This one's fast: get the rain up and sweep with Swift Swim

subs.name: Rain balance
subs.plan: This one's steadier: the rain powers the Water attacks while the bulkier members hold on

archetypes.name: Sun
archetypes.plan: Drought or Sunny Day brings harsh sunlight for 5 rounds (8 with a Heat Rock): Fire moves hit ×1.5 and Water moves ×0.5, Chlorophyll doubles Speed, and Solar Beam and Solar Blade fire the same turn at ×1.5

subs.name: Drought offense
subs.plan: The Drought Pokémon brings the sun just by coming in

subs.name: Chlorophyll offense
subs.plan: In the sun the Chlorophyll sweepers outspeed nearly everything

archetypes.name: Sand
archetypes.plan: Sandstorm lasts 5 rounds (8 with a Smooth Rock): everything but Rock, Ground and Steel types loses 1/16 of its HP a turn, Rock types get ×1.5 Sp. Def, Sand Rush doubles Speed and Sand Force powers up Rock, Ground and Steel moves

subs.name: Sand Rush offense
subs.plan: Sand Rush or Sand Force does the damage in the storm

subs.name: Sand balance
subs.plan: The storm wears foes down while sturdy Rock and Ground types take the hits

archetypes.name: Snow
archetypes.plan: hail and snow are one weather here, 5 rounds (8 with an Icy Rock): everything but Ice types loses 1/16 of its HP a turn, Ice types get ×1.5 Defense, Blizzard never misses, and Aurora Veil can go up

subs.name: Aurora Veil offense
subs.plan: Aurora Veil cuts the damage the team takes while the attackers go to work

subs.name: Blizzard spam
subs.plan: Blizzard never misses in hail and hits every foe at once

archetypes.name: Trick Room
archetypes.plan: Trick Room flips the turn order for 5 rounds, so the slowest Pokémon move first and slow heavy hitters do the damage

subs.name: Hard Trick Room
subs.plan: Everyone's slow, so the whole team wants the room up, and the setter's Quick Claw gets it up first

subs.name: Semi-Room
subs.plan: A mix: slow hitters for the room, and a few that work without it

archetypes.name: Tailwind
archetypes.plan: Tailwind doubles the whole team's Speed for 4 rounds, so the attackers get their turns first

subs.name: Tailwind offense
subs.plan: All-out attack while the tailwind blows; the setter's Quick Claw gets it going first

subs.name: Tailwind balance
subs.plan: Tailwind plus a few Pokémon that hold up once it runs out

archetypes.name: Hyper Offense
archetypes.plan: hit hard and fast, before the other side gets to set anything up

subs.name: Dual Screens
subs.plan: The first screen setter holds the Quick Claw (and a priority move if it has one) to get Reflect and Light Screen up first, the second holds Light Clay for 8 rounds, and the sweepers boost behind them

subs.name: Setup chain
subs.plan: A fast lead with the Quick Claw lays hazards first, then setup sweepers boost and clean up

subs.name: Priority rush
subs.plan: Three leads with priority attacks: each one is +30% turn meter the moment they're sent out, and they stack, so the team moves first and keeps hitting

archetypes.name: Bulky Offense
archetypes.plan: strong attackers that can take a hit too, so the team wins the trades

subs.name: Intimidate core
subs.plan: An Intimidate Pokémon lowers the foes' Attack as it comes in, so physical attackers hit softer

subs.name: Pivot core
subs.plan: Pivots bring the right Pokémon in for each matchup

subs.name: Pledge core
subs.plan: The Kanto starters' Pledges: a teammate's different Pledge since your last turn makes yours a 150-power combined move, with a sea of fire, a swamp or a rainbow

archetypes.name: Balance
archetypes.plan: a bit of everything: a bulky Pokémon with recovery, entry hazards, a pivot, and strong attackers to win with

subs.name: Hazard balance
subs.plan: Entry hazards wear down every Pokémon that switches in

subs.name: Pivot balance
subs.plan: Pivots keep the right matchup on the field

archetypes.name: Stall
archetypes.plan: bulky walls with recovery, status and entry hazards wear the other side down slowly

subs.name: Full stall
subs.plan: Everything is about outlasting

subs.name: Semi-stall
subs.plan: Walls, plus a bulky attacker to finish things

archetypes.name: Volt-Turn
archetypes.plan: pivots hit and switch out with U-turn, Volt Switch or Flip Turn, bringing hard hitters in on good matchups. Careful, Pursuit hits a pivot before it gets out

subs.name: Choice pivots
subs.plan: Choice items power up the pivots (no move lock here)

subs.name: Pivot balance
subs.plan: Pivots keep the right matchup on the field

archetypes.name: Follow Me
archetypes.plan: a redirector pulls the attacks onto itself with Follow Me or Rage Powder while the sweepers set up safely

subs.name: Follow Me setup
subs.plan: Follow Me buys the setup turns

subs.name: Rage Powder offense
subs.plan: Rage Powder buys the turns for the attackers

archetypes.name: Fake Out + Intimidate
archetypes.plan: Fake Out makes a foe flinch, Intimidate lowers the foes' Attack, and strong attackers do the rest

subs.name: Goodstuffs
subs.plan: Just strong Pokémon that work well together

subs.name: Spread offense
subs.plan: Spread moves hit every foe at once, 75% each
